justification_text:
My point estimates across all three horizons are clustered tightly around 559–565, reflecting a view that the underlying variable is in a relatively stable regime with only modest drift expected over time. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 559 is essentially anchored to the most recent observed level, assuming mean-reverting dynamics and no imminent catalyst for a sharp move. At one week, the slight uptick to 561 reflects a small positive drift assumption, perhaps based on a modest trend or seasonal pattern. At one month, the estimate of 565 continues that gentle upward drift, suggesting I expected gradual appreciation or growth rather than a flat or declining trajectory. The consistency across horizons implies I saw no strong regime-change signal that would justify a larger directional adjustment.

The confidence interval widths expand predictably as the horizon lengthens, which is standard behavior under most time-series models where uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans only 34 units (542–576), reflecting that short-term fluctuations are relatively constrained and recent volatility was moderate. By one week, the interval widens to 58 units (532–590), incorporating the possibility of a few consecutive adverse or favorable sessions. At one month, the interval opens up to 120 units (505–625), acknowledging that over roughly 20 trading days, a wide range of economic prints, policy signals, and sentiment shifts could accumulate into a meaningful deviation from the point estimate. The interval widths suggest I was working with an annualized volatility in a moderate range, consistent with a relatively stable but not dormant asset or index.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside even the one-month interval include sudden macroeconomic shocks such as a surprise inflation print, an unexpected central bank policy shift, or a geopolitical escalation that triggers a risk-off episode. On the upside, stronger-than-expected earnings, a dovish policy pivot, or a resolution of an ongoing uncertainty could drive values above 625. On the downside, a liquidity event, credit stress, or a sharp deterioration in forward guidance could breach the 505 floor. These tail risks are by definition underweighted in a 90% confidence interval, so roughly one-in-ten outcomes should be expected to fall outside the stated bounds even under normal model assumptions.
